title: Exclusion: Irradiated Zone Sound Effects
shortText: 103 post apocalyptic sound effects: a Geiger counter by dose, hazmat kit, rust and scrap, radio, zone beds. WAV + OGG.
html:
An exclusion zone in sound: a Geiger counter you set by dose, and the dead town around it

103 post apocalyptic sound effects: a Geiger counter at 8 dose levels from a few ticks to a roar, a dosimeter, the hazmat kit, rust and scrap struck three ways, steam, acid and live cables, footsteps on rubble, glass and catwalks, a shortwave radio, five places as stackable beds and 28 seamless loops.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No credit required. No revenue limit, no unit cap, no second licence to buy later if your game does well. Use it in as many projects as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell the sounds themselves as sounds. The full plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy paste credit line if you want one.

Everything is synthesised from code. No recordings, no sample libraries, no third party clips, so there is no upstream licence behind this one and nobody can content ID claim these sounds against your project.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 22 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. Three dose levels from across the ladder, one steel pipe on all four materials, the dosimeter at all three severities, a place with both of its layers, and the counter switching on, off and dying.

What is in it

  • Geiger counter (15)
  • Dosimeter (7)
  • Hazmat kit (15)
  • Rust and scrap (29)
  • Hazards (11)
  • Underfoot (8)
  • Radio (8)
  • Places (10)

A Geiger counter you set by dose

8 seamless loops, one per dose level, from 0.75 clicks a second to 150. Each is what a Geiger counter tube actually produces: a random click train at a set average rate, with the tube's own dead time, through the counter's small speaker. Map your radiation value to a level and play that loop. The clicks in every shipped loop were counted from the audio and match the design, and each level has at least 1.5 times the clicks of the one below, so the ladder you hear is the ladder the table says. Plus the counter switching on and off, an approach and a retreat sweep, sudden spikes and the battery dying.

Rust and scrap, struck three ways

A boot kick, a steel pipe and a thrown stone against corrugated sheet, an oil drum, rebar and a chain-link fence. The striker changes the sound on every material and the material changes it for every striker: 18 material pairs and 12 striker pairs measured apart on the shipped files, 0 too close. Around it: sheet metal rattling in the wind, a fence climbed and shaken, rusted hatches and doors, scrap, debris, a rolling drum, a manhole cover and a stuck valve.

The kit, the radio and five places

The hazmat kit (suit rustle, crouch and stand, a filter unscrewed and seated, the mask clicked home, boot covers, gloves, a decontamination shower), the dosimeter (three severities, each brighter than the last, single pitches rather than a tune), a shortwave radio without voices, and five places, a dead city, an irradiated forest, a reactor hall, a bunker and an ash plain, each a bed and a detail layer of one length that stack (10 stacks re-summed from the shipped files). Three lifecycles, the counter, the shower and the radio, ship as start, loop and stop (10 states, every loop flag read out of the file).

Already own our other packs?

Where this pack fills a role Escapement, Ship Systems, Upheaval, Leeward, Portcullis, Unseen, Backward, Iron Road, Dwell, Pithead or Footfall already fills (steam, static, sparks, a hatch, an iron door, an alarm, debris, a step on metal), the two were measured against each other from both packs' files: 26 shared roles, every one a different sound.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a manifest listing every file by slot.
  • 28 seamless loops with sample accurate loop points in the WAV and the OGG. Checked in a blank Godot 4 project: the WAV

loops import looping with default settings.

  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 4.79 dB. The sparsest Geiger levels sit quieter than the rest by design.
  • pack_proof.json ships with the pack: 967 checks, 0 failed.
  • No voices, no breathing, no creatures and nothing musical, so it sits under any score.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds, not recordings of a real counter or a real zone. The measurements above are signal measurements and counted clicks, not a claim that it sounds good. That is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Concrete: Urban and Liminal Place Beds, empty car parks, stairwells and service tunnels as layered beds.
  • Upheaval: Natural Disasters, earthquakes, eruptions and storms as layers you drive with one value.
  • Haulage: Vehicles, Motors and Industrial Machines, engines and machines from start to strain to stop.
